transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-15 10:00 PT, Duration 46m
Attendees: Arielle Park (Redwood AE), Devon Li (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Novapay Head of ML), Elena Gomez (Novapay Platform), Jordan Reeves (Novapay SRE)

[00:00] Arielle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll jump in. This is the weekly POC sync for throughput optimization, just a quick recap — Devon and I from Redwood, and Samir, Elena, Jordan from Novapay.
[00:18] Samir: Yep thanks Arielle. Quick note, our infra people had a brief outage this morning, so apologies if my audio drops.
[00:25] Devon: No worries. Quick agenda: review last week's run where we tuned continuous batching and adjusted concurrency from 8 to 12, show current numbers, then decisions on queueing and next stress test.
[00:38] Elena: Sounds good. We want to hit at least 10k tokens/sec sustained in p95 under our demo traffic shape, and keep p95 under 350ms otherwise product folks will push back.
[00:50] Arielle: Yeah that's the SLA target I jotted down. Okay Devon, can you walk through the numbers?
[00:55] [01:00] Devon: Sure; so last run we enabled continuous batching with a 20ms coalesce window and a max batch size of 64. Observed aggregate tokens/sec went from ~6.2k to ~9.1k, p50 latency improved from 80ms to 60ms, p95 was at 310ms — which is closer to Elena's target. However tail p99 is still spiky around 820ms in peak bursts.
[01:30] Samir: Is that on the hosted pool or the dedicated test nodes?
[01:34] Devon: This was on the dedicated pilot pool you gave us (4x A100 equivalents), with the Redwood runtime set to dynamic KV cache and no quant changes. Note: some transcriber labels may show Redwood Dedicaed in the logs, small typo, but config is the dedicated pool.
[01:48] Jordan: We're curious about how queueing behaved — did requests queue at the runtime or in our ingress LB? We saw some 502s during the ramp.
[01:57] Devon: Good question. Most queueing happened in the runtime's request queue; we also hit a soft limit on concurrency at the pod side. The 502s correlate with a short spike where our LB retried and upstream returned connection resets. We recommend adjusting the LB timeout and enabling in-flight request draining — that should reduce 502s.
[02:18] Elena: For the batch settings, what was the average batch size distribution? We need to understand variability.
[02:24] Devon: Right — average batch size was 38, median 36, but 90th percentile reached 52 when traffic was bursty. I'll attach the distribution chart. There's also a small mismatch in the logs where some request IDs look like UUIDs truncated which made mapping a bit noisy.
[02:40] Samir: That matches what we saw. The production traffic shape has many short prompts and occasional long prompts that blow up token counts. How does the runtime prioritize short-vs-long so long prompts don't block short ones?
[02:55] Devon: By default the runtime does FIFO with a small age-based bump — but we can enable short-first scheduling which selects smaller sequence-length requests to fill batches earlier. That reduces tail latency for short requests at the expense of slightly lower batch fill efficiency for long-only windows.
[03:15] Arielle: Tradeoff question: do we prefer slightly lower tokens/sec but more predictable p95 or max throughput with higher tails? Which does Novapay prefer?
[03:25] Samir: We prefer predictable p95 under 350ms. Peak throughput is less important than consistent latency for UX. So short-first scheduling sounds good.
[03:33] Devon: Okay we'll try short-first. Also we can tighten the coalesce window down to 15ms for this traffic shape; that improved p95 on one of our runs but reduced peak tokens/sec by ~6%.
[03:45] Jordan: Network-wise we can increase LB timeout by 250ms and enable retry jitter. We'll coordinate with Elena to make that change on staging.
[03:54] Elena: I'll do that after the call.
[04:00] [04:12] Devon: On concurrency, we bumped concurrency target from 8 to 12 last week. When we moved to 16 in a short test, tokens/sec improved to ~11.7k but p99 worsened. The sweet spot for your traffic looked like 12-14 concurrency. We also saw higher GPU utilization >85% at 16 which could risk overheating on long runs.
[04:34] Samir: Can we set an auto-scaling policy that keeps concurrency at 12 but allows brief bursts to 16 with a cooling period?
[04:40] Devon: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports a burst capacity policy; we can configure a short window, e.g., 120s burst to 16 with an enforced cooldown to 300s. Cost-wise, that does have implications — Arielle can share pricing impact.
[04:55] Arielle: I'll include a pricing estimate. Roughly, burst to 16 for brief windows adds ~18% to committed hours in our model, but we can model by actual minutes used.
[05:07] [05:20] Samir: About caching — we saw some prefix cache hits but not as many as expected. Any tips?
[05:26] Devon: We noticed your prompt template has high variability, low prefix reuse. A few suggestions: canonicalize prompt prefixes, move stable context to system messages (where caching is more effective), and enable KV prewarm for model hot starts. These together moved our effective token reuse from 12% to 28% in tests.
[05:45] Elena: We can try canonicalization; I'll coordinate with the product team.
[05:49] Jordan: Quick Q on security — we need to confirm KMS flows if we move to dedicated. Any blockers?
[05:55] Arielle: No blockers; Redwood Dedicated supports customer KMS via our private deployment options. We'll send SOC2 docs and encryption flow diagrams.
[06:04] [06:15] Devon: Back to batching — there's an idea to use adaptive batch size capped by latency budget per request class. So high-priority low-latency requests get small cap, background reranks get large cap. That requires request tagging and route policy in the gateway.
[06:32] Samir: We can tag requests by priority from the app layer. We'll add a header X-NOVAPAY-PRIORITY.
[06:39] Arielle: Great. That allows mixed workload optimization which matches your production shape.
[06:44] [07:00] Devon: On queueing policy: we can implement a per-route queue with backpressure and a shed-below-threshold policy to protect tail latency. Essentially if queue length exceeds N, low-priority requests get 429.
[07:18] Jordan: We'd prefer graceful shedding rather than hard 429s — maybe return a small fallback or cached summary.
[07:25] Devon: Yep we can configure a policy to return cached placeholder when available; otherwise 429 is the fallback.
[07:31] Samir: Good.
[07:35] [07:50] Arielle: Quick check — security docs and SOC2 will be in your inbox. Also Devon will run a longer stress test next week. Any other blockers?
[07:58] Samir: One question on observability — how granular are the batch-level traces? We need request-to-batch mapping for debugging.
[08:06] Devon: We emit per-batch metrics and include request IDs in batch logs. There's a small issue where some client IDs got truncated in our previous instrumented logs — we'll ensure full IDs are present.
[08:18] Elena: That will help.
[08:22] [09:00] Devon: I'll summarize recommended config changes: enable short-first scheduling, reduce coalesce to 15ms, keep target concurrency at 12 with burst to 16 (120s/300s cooldown), enable per-route priority tagging and backpressure, increase LB timeouts.
[09:19] Samir: Sounds right. Is there any quantization we should consider? We want quality to remain high.
[09:25] Devon: For now we didn't change quant; we can test 4-bit quant on a shadow run — quality regression was minimal for your LLM family in our internal tests but we should validate.
[09:36] Arielle: We'll add a shadow quant test to the plan.
[09:40] [10:15] Samir: On timelines, if we run the 2-hour stress test and see consistent p95 < 350ms, how soon can we flip to dedicated?
[10:24] Arielle: Typically after we validate runs and do the pilot acceptance criteria, we can schedule a dedicated capacity reservation in 2-3 weeks depending on region availability. We'll coordinate with procurement.
[10:34] Samir: Ok procurement will want a TCO and SLA.
[10:39] Arielle: I'll send a pricing + SLA note.
[10:42] [12:00] Devon: One minor note — some of the monitoring dashboards showed token accounting discrepancies; likely due to double-counting in edge retries. We'll patch that in telemetry and re-run the accounting overnight.
[12:15] Elena: Good to know.
[12:18] [13:00] Samir: Anything else on queueing?
[13:05] Devon: We'll implement soft queue limits with priority-aware shedding and include a fallback header so clients get a reason code.
[13:13] Jordan: Perfect.
[13:16] [15:00] Arielle: Ok let's recap and confirm action items. Devon — 2-hour stress test with short-first scheduling + coalesce 15ms + concurrency 12/burst16, include batch size distribution and p50/p95/p99, due 4/18. Samir — provide production traffic sample and SLA, due 4/17. Elena — update LB timeouts on staging and confirm network rules. Arielle — send pricing and SOC2 docs, and benchmark spreadsheet.
[15:46] Samir: Confirmed. One more ask: can Redwood share a simple runbook for when we hit tail spikes? Our SREs want steps.
[15:55] Devon: We'll draft a runbook: immediate steps (reduce concurrency, enable short-first, drain that pod) and longer-term fixes.
[16:03] Arielle: We'll attach that to the follow-up email.
[16:07] [16:30] Jordan: Thanks all.
[16:32] Elena: Thanks.
[16:34] Arielle: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and next steps.
[16:38] Samir: Bye.

End of transcript.
